quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This lets you see areas your mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: If you see other drivers acting angry, you should:

options.text: Avoid making eye contact with them.
Not make hand gestures at them.

questions.explanation: Keep yourself safe by staying away from angry drivers. Do not make eye contact or use hand gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you can to avoid them.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you only drink a little.

questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is very dangerous. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs. It puts both you and others at risk.

questions.question: Road rage is:

options.text: An okay response to bad drivers.

questions.explanation: Road rage is a criminal offense. When a small traffic problem turns into an angry confrontation, drivers can face legal charges.

questions.question: When should you fasten your safety belt?
questions.explanation: You and all passengers must wear safety belts before the car starts. Make sure everyone has their belt fastened before you drive.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your chance of an accident.
Making you fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others.

questions.explanation: Strong emotions hurt your driving. If you feel worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you cannot focus well on driving. It is better to wait until you feel calm.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway:

options.text: Exit at the next exit and come back.
Roll down your window and ask another driver for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and come back.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on a highway. Exit at the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces your driving skills. It makes you react slowly and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. At a stop sign, you must stop completely. Check for pedestrians and cross traffic. Wait for the intersection to clear before you go.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights if you have them. High beams bounce off fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws as if there were no construction.

questions.explanation: Follow directions from flaggers, signs, and police officers in construction zones. Failure to do so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as well in the dark.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use appropriate headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Pass faster downhill than smaller vehicles.
Turn with a smaller radius than smaller vehicles.
Pass faster uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because of their size and weight, trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Leave the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you cannot stay awake, get off the road and nap. Drowsy driving is dangerous for you and others.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal three to five seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before you reach the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians. Turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is showing red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is showing green.
A traffic signal is coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is coming up.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: You should use evasive steering when:

options.text: Making normal steering adjustments while driving.
Avoiding a hazard while driving at high speed.
Backing up, signaling, using the radio, or using windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoiding a hazard while driving at high speed.
questions.explanation: At high speeds, even small steering changes move your vehicle left or right quickly. When brakes lock or your vehicle leaves the road, use careful steering to stay in your lane. Do not overcorrect, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive with caution.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
You can drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells drivers that an island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must stay to the right of it.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Avoid using cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What does the "E" in SIPDE stand for?
questions.explanation: The "E" in SIPDE stands for "Execute a move." When you face a dangerous situation, you should brake, speed up, turn, or make another move.

questions.question: In Louisiana, who must wear a safety belt?
questions.explanation: Louisiana law requires all people in a vehicle to wear a safety belt. It is the most effective safety device in cars.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to an upcoming traffic light. Be ready for red, yellow, or green lights and cross traffic.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when you:

options.text: Stare at the road for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stare at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare straight ahead at the road for too long and stop looking around. You may zone out and miss traffic slowing down or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other cars are present.
Must be followed only when police are nearby.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired on a long drive, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break to prevent fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and take a nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, use ____ to show you are turning.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show other drivers that you are turning.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, as long as a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look carefully in both directions first.

questions.explanation: Red flashing lights, lowered gates, and bells at railroad crossings mean you must stop completely. Wait until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised before crossing. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front suddenly slows or stops, you may not have enough time to stop and avoid hitting it.

questions.question: What can make a driver unable to drive safely?
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires the driver to be in good physical and mental condition. Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and being tired can all affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead where another road crosses.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop and may skid on sharp turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: When can drivers pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder?

options.text: When the car in front is waiting to turn left.
When the car in front is driving under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder, whether it is paved or not. Other drivers will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder and hit your vehicle.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road makes a sharp right turn ahead.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: A sudden change in weather means you need to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Pay special attention to vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, you must adjust how you drive. Always slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them so they will not cross against red lights again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians and other cars that may be in the intersection, even if you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians in every situation.
